text:
alex: Heads-up — our nightly replay harness shows a weird perf regression vs the synthetic bench after the kernel-selection change.
maria: ugh, details? regression on p99 or throughput?
sam: p50 fine, p95 ~+10%, p99 spikes up to +40% on short requests (avg seq 32). Synthetic bench (many persistent connections) doesn't show this.
jni: probably connection churn + KV cold misses? Did the replay open new sockets per request?
alex: replay uses per-session recorded timelines, many short-lived sessions. The synthetic harness uses long-lived keep-alive pools. When we flipped to the new attention kernel heuristic it started choosing the fallback path for short sequences in some hardware combos.
perf-bot: perf report attached: `baseline=120ms p99; candidate=168ms p99; throughput ~-2%`.
maria: interesting — fallback kernel is slightly faster on synthetic because batching grows, but with lots of tiny TCP bursts TLS/Nagle latency shows up and hides batching gains.
sam: can we repro locally by forcing connection churn? command I used: `wrk2 -t8 -c200 --timeout 5s -d60s --script replay.lua` where replay.lua simulates short sessions.
jni: reproduced. When I toggle TCP_NODELAY off I see 1-5ms extra per request tail on Linux due to Nagle coalescing on small writes.
alex: so root cause is interplay: (1) kernel selection changed which expects more steady batching, (2) replay pattern prevents batching and warms KV cache poorly, (3) socket behavior adds micro-latency.
maria: solution ideas:
- enforce keepalive/connection-pool settings in replay harness to get apples-to-apples with synthetic
- add a replay mode that preserves original connection lifetimes vs a "many-short-sessions" mode
- instrument runtime to tag requests with `conn_reuse=true|false` and include in perf dashboards
- for kernel selection: add a fast-path check for cold-KV / low-batch conditions to prefer the old kernel
sam: also add a small toggle in the bench client to disable Nagle and force TLS session reuse so we can separate transport vs runtime.
jni: I ran a flamegraph: most extra time is in `ssl_write` + `tcp_output` + `batch_scheduler` wait when connections are single-request. Attaching slice: `ssl_write 35% -> tcp_output 20% -> batch_wait 25%`.
perf-bot: note: a lot of our CI synthetic runs set `--conn-pool=dynamic` which masks churn. We should add an "apples-to-apples" suite that compares both client behaviors.
alex: agree. I'll: (1) add conn_reuse tagging, (2) add replay harness mode preserving original socket patterns, (3) add kernel fallback heuristic for low-batch/cold-KV.
maria: can you also add a short doc with recommended client settings (keepalive, pool=1-4 per core, TCP_NODELAY=true, TLS session resumption) so customers can reproduce? small blurb in docs/benching.
sam: quick temporary mitigation: enable our fallback kernel when detected `batch_wait_time > 3ms` and `active_batch_size < 4` — that kills the p99 while we validate.
alex: I'll open a PR with the runtime guard and replay harness changes. tagging @jni to review perf traces. Thanks all :thumbsup:
